input.question: Explain why a binary search tree can lose its logarithmic performance, and how self-balancing trees prevent this. (10 marks)
input.rubric: 4 marks: sorted/skewed insertions make the tree degenerate into a linked list with linear height. 3 marks: operations cost is proportional to height. 3 marks: self-balancing trees (AVL/red-black) use rotations to keep height logarithmic.
input.student_answer: If keys are inserted in sorted order every new node goes to the right, so the tree becomes a linked list and search becomes O(n) because cost depends on height. AVL and red-black trees rotate nodes after insertions and deletions to keep the height O(log n).

input.question: Describe how round-robin scheduling works and explain the effect of choosing a very small or very large time quantum. (10 marks)
input.rubric: 4 marks: each process gets a fixed quantum and goes to the back of the ready queue when it expires. 3 marks: very small quantum causes high context-switch overhead. 3 marks: very large quantum degenerates to first-come first-served.
input.student_answer: Each ready process runs for one time quantum; if it has not finished it is preempted and placed at the end of the ready queue. A tiny quantum means the CPU spends much of its time context switching, while a huge quantum makes round-robin behave like FCFS with poor response time.

input.question: Describe how round-robin scheduling works and explain the effect of choosing a very small or very large time quantum. (10 marks)

input.student_answer: Processes take turns for a fixed time slice. Small slices waste time switching. Big slices are like FCFS.

input.student_answer: The scheduler keeps a circular queue and each process gets a quantum before preemption. If the quantum is too small, overhead from saving and restoring state dominates. If it is too large, interactive processes wait a long time.

input.question: Explain how TCP achieves reliable delivery and how slow start and congestion avoidance control the sending rate. (10 marks)
input.rubric: 4 marks: sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmission on timeout/duplicate ACKs. 3 marks: slow start grows the congestion window exponentially up to a threshold. 3 marks: congestion avoidance grows linearly and loss reduces the window.
input.student_answer: TCP numbers bytes and the receiver acknowledges them; missing data is retransmitted after a timeout or three duplicate ACKs. Slow start doubles the congestion window every RTT until the threshold, then congestion avoidance adds one segment per RTT, and on loss the window is cut.

input.student_answer: TCP uses acknowledgements and resends lost packets. Slow start increases the window quickly and then it increases slowly.

input.question: Describe two-phase locking and explain why strict two-phase locking is used in practice. (10 marks)
input.rubric: 4 marks: growing phase acquires locks, shrinking phase releases; no lock acquired after any release. 3 marks: guarantees conflict-serialisable schedules. 3 marks: strict 2PL holds exclusive locks until commit, preventing cascading aborts.
input.student_answer: In 2PL a transaction has a growing phase where it acquires locks and a shrinking phase where it releases them, and it cannot acquire any lock after releasing one. This guarantees serialisable schedules. Strict 2PL keeps exclusive locks until commit or abort so no other transaction reads uncommitted data, avoiding cascading aborts.

input.question: Describe two-phase locking and explain why strict two-phase locking is used in practice. (10 marks)

input.student_answer: Two phase locking means locks are taken first and released later. Strict 2PL keeps locks until commit.

input.question: Describe two-phase locking and explain why strict two-phase locking is used in practice. (10 marks)
input.rubric: 4 marks: growing phase acquires locks, shrinking phase releases; no lock acquired after any release. 3 marks: guarantees conflict-serialisable schedules. 3 marks: strict 2PL holds exclusive locks until commit, preventing cascading aborts.
input.student_answer: A transaction acquires all needed locks before releasing any. This makes schedules serialisable. The strict version holds write locks until the end so aborts do not cascade.
